title: Hollow and Thorn
premise: Mara Brightwater, a mercenary bound by oath to a god that has gone silent, earns her living guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, she shelters a fugitive memory-keeper named Ilen whose magic can open the Hollow Door—the only exit from Thornfell, a country that was erased from maps and memory generations ago. As soldiers close in and her sworn order demands she surrender him, Mara must choose between the duty that defines her and the found family forming around their desperate caravan. In the end, she breaks her oath to the silent god, sacrifices her own memories of home to power the Door, and sends Ilen and their companions through—remaining behind as the new guardian of a country only she now remembers.
about_author: Noor Eastwick is the pen name of a former cartographer's apprentice who grew up in mining towns at the edge of real mountain ranges, where old roads outlasted the names of the villages they served. They write fantasy about borders, oaths, and the people who carry places in their heads after the places are gone.

chapters.title: The Silent Bell
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On a smuggling run through Thornfell, Mara prays at a roadside shrine to her god and receives no answer for the hundredth time. She guides a merchant convoy past a crown checkpoint and sees new bounty broadsheets: anyone with the gift is to be taken alive. The beat is quiet unease—a world tilting.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Switchback
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She finds Ilen half-frozen above the treeline, hunted by crown wardens, his memory-gift flickering like a dying lamp. Against every mercenary instinct, she hides him in an abandoned watch-shrine. The beat is reluctant compassion; her oath says turn him in, her gut says otherwise.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Ilen's POV. Fleeing together, they reach the village of Cinderhollow, where gifted folk have already been taken and their houses burned. Ilen reveals he can open the Hollow Door—but only if he can remember how, and someone has been eating his memories from afar. The beat is grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Company of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They gather fellow fugitives: Brannic, a disgraced warden who deserted rather than arrest children; Sefa, a deaf herb-witch; and Pip, a pickpocket child with a faint gift of luck. Around a fire in a smuggler's cave, they become something like a family. The beat is warmth earned against fear.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Reading bone-casts, Sefa confirms the moon will complete its thirteenth turn in six weeks—when the Door closes for another century. Meanwhile Mara's sworn order finds her and demands Ilen's surrender, invoking the oath that binds her body and tongue. The beat is the noose tightening.

chapters.title: The Oath's Teeth
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The oath physically drags Mara toward betrayal; she fights it through the night while Ilen, half-dreaming, unknowingly shares his memories with her—and she glimpses the erased country of Thornfell as it was. The beat is intimate and terrible: love arriving exactly when duty turns predatory.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Crown wardens trap the company at a mountain pass. Brannic faces his former brothers-in-arms; Pip is nearly taken before Mara breaks part of her oath at terrible cost—her god answers for the first time in years, furious. The beat is sacrifice and schism: the company escapes, wounded and scattered.

chapters.title: The Country That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ilen's POV. Sheltered in the ruins of old Thornfell's capital, Ilen recovers stolen memories and learns the truth: the crown erased the country itself, and the silent god is Thornfell's forgotten patron, muted by the same spell. The Door requires a willing memory-sacrifice. The beat is revelation and dread.

chapters.title: Hollow and Thorn
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With one day left, wardens besiege the capital ruins. Mara chooses: she offers her own memories of home and childhood to wake the god and open the Door, trading her past for the company's future. The climax is a battle, a breaking oath, and a door of light opening in the mountain's heart.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Ilen and the others pass through; Ilen leaves her a single returned memory—his face, their fire, the word 'stay remembered.' Mara remains as the Door's guardian, the last person who knows Thornfell existed, writing its name on stones so it can't be erased twice. The beat is bittersweet peace: family kept, self remade.
